title: Writing +, − and =
short: Write a number sentence that matches a story or picture.
trouble: Children think the equals sign means "write the answer now," not "is the same amount as."

blocks.html: You can put together, take away and write numerals. A number sentence tells the story with numbers and signs.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: 4 + 1 and 5 are the same amount, so the balance is level: $4 + 1 = 5$.

blocks.html: $+$ means put together. $-$ means take away. $=$ means “is the same amount as.”
The equals sign works like a balance. Both sides must be the same amount. That is why $5 = 4 + 1$ is true too: the answer can come first.

blocks.title: Frogs hop away
blocks.q: Write a number sentence: 5 frogs sit on a log. 2 hop away. 3 are left.
steps: Hopping away is taking away, so use $-$.

blocks.html: Thinking = means “write the answer now.” It means “is the same amount as.” So $4 + 1 = 5$ and $5 = 4 + 1$ are both true.
For grown-ups: Sometimes read = aloud as “is the same amount as,” so your child hears what it really means.
